headline: Gulf State Park Lodging and Trail Access
reservation: Reservations for the Gulf State Park Lodge or the improved campground should be secured months in advance for spring and summer peaks. While beach access is plentiful, parking at popular trailheads like the Backcountry Trail can reach capacity, requiring visitors to check local city parking apps or official park signage.

days.title: Ecosystems and Inland Waterways

stops.name: Hugh S. Branyon Backcountry Trail
stops.detail: Cycle through six distinct habitats, including maritime forests and dunes, looking for resident gopher tortoises.

stops.name: Lake Shelby
stops.detail: Paddle this freshwater lake located just hundreds of yards from the saltwater Gulf to see the coastal hydrological balance.

days.driving: Allow 15–30 minutes within the park; conditions vary
days.note: Paved trails are suitable for walking or cycling, but lack shade in midday summer heat.

days.title: Wildlife Refuges and Coastal Defense

stops.name: Bon Secour National Wildlife Refuge
stops.detail: Hike the Pine Beach Trail to see the habitat of the Alabama beach mouse and diverse migratory birds.

stops.name: Fort Morgan
stops.detail: Visit the western tip of the peninsula to explore the tunnels of this historic masonry fort at the mouth of Mobile Bay.

days.driving: Allow 45–60 minutes to reach the western terminus; conditions vary
days.note: The road to Fort Morgan is a two-lane stretch; expect slower paces during peak fishing seasons.

days.title: The Wharf and Bay Excursions

stops.name: The Wharf at Orange Beach
stops.detail: Explore the local waterfront district for maritime shopping and views of the Intracoastal Waterway.

stops.name: Gulf State Park Pier
stops.detail: Walk the extended pier to observe local angling and search for rays in the turquoise shallows below.

days.driving: Allow 30–50 minutes for regional loops; conditions vary
days.note: Check the pier status for recent maintenance updates, as storm damage can affect access.

intel.title: Public Beach Access
intel.text: City-managed lots in Gulf Shores use a paid parking system. Use official mobile apps to monitor time and avoid fines at popular boardwalk entrances.

intel.title: Dauphin Island Ferry
intel.text: The Mobile Bay Ferry connects Fort Morgan to Dauphin Island. This service is weather-dependent and requires checking the daily schedule for current vessel status.

intel.title: Turtle Nesting Seasons
intel.text: Between May and October, beach activity is subject to turtle nesting protections. Avoid using white flashlights and remove all gear from the sand by sunset.

intel.title: Gateway Amenities
intel.text: Foley and Gulf Shores offer abundant fueling stations and supplies. Once traveling west toward Fort Morgan, commercial services become extremely limited.

intel.title: Refuge Connectivity
intel.text: Cellular signal is strong in the town centers but often drops within the interior of Bon Secour. Carry physical maps when hiking the refuge's maritime trails.

plan.arrival: Drive from Pensacola (PNS) and stop in Foley for grocery supplies before checking into your coastal rental or park lodge.
plan.vehicle: Standard cars are suitable for all paved roads; bicycles are highly recommended for the 28-mile trail network.
plan.goldenHour: The Gulf State Park Pier is a primary viewpoint for watching the sun set over the Gulf, though colors vary by humidity levels.
